metadata.title: On the construction of non-$2$-colorable uniform hypergraphs

extraction_notes.note: Tables 1 and 2 list best-known bounds on m(n) for n<=17 (including m(13)<=297347 and m(17)<=13201419, stated only in Table 2); table rows were not made nodes.
The custom 'Result' environment has no standard type; typed theorem, since these are the paper's main stated results, proved later by the hyperedge counts and Lemmas 3-5.

Results 1-3 are restated verbatim in Sections 3-5 after the counting arguments; the restated inequalities got no node (one node per repeated statement) and the counting paragraphs became prose proofs of the Result environments.

Sections 3-5 repeat the Section 2 notation sentences (m_{n-2}, Y, U, V, matching vertices, U_K, V_K, complements), Section 5 with n=8; these restatements got no nodes and the Section 2 definitions carry the edges.
Each hypergraph construction (steps (i)-(vii)) could be a definition of H; typed algorithm per the step-by-step procedure rule, one algorithm_step per listed step.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{firstlemma}
Consider a coloring $\chi$ of the hypergraph $H$ having the property that there does not exist two different \textit{matching pairs} of vertices ($u_i,v_i^p$) and ($u_j,v_j^p$) in any of the set-ordered set pair ($U,V^p$) such that $u_i$ and $v_i^p$ are colored with Red, and, $u_j$ and $v_j^p$ are colored with Blue in $\chi$. Then, $\chi$ is not a proper $2$-coloring of $H$.
nodes.clean_text: Consider a coloring chi of the hypergraph H having the property that there does not exist two different matching pairs of vertices (u_i,v_i^p) and (u_j,v_j^p) in any of the set-ordered set pair (U,V^p) such that u_i and v_i^p are colored with Red, and, u_j and v_j^p are colored with Blue in chi. Then, chi is not a proper 2-coloring of H.
nodes.label: firstlemma

nodes.statement: Assume for the sake of contradiction that chi is a proper 2-coloring of H. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that there is no matching pair (u_i,v_i^p) in the set-ordered set pair (U,V^p) such that both u_i and v_i^p are colored by Red. Let U_K denote the set of vertices in U which are Red in this coloring, where K subseteq \1, 2, ldots n\ denotes the set of indices of the vertices in the set U_K. Note that U_K must be a proper subset of U, as U is one of the hyperedges of H. Let us consider the following 2 cases: item Case 1: 1 leq |U_K| < lfloor n/2rfloor If |U_K| is even, then consider the hyperedge V_K^p cup barU_K. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If |U_K| is odd, then consider the hyperedge U_K cup barV_K^p. At least one of the vertices, say v_l^p in barV_K^p, must have been colored Blue in chi. Consider the vertex u_l such that (u_l,v_l^p) is a matching pair of vertices in (U,V^p). It can be seen that the hyperedge V_K^p cup barU_K cup \v_l^p\ setminus \u_l\ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. item Case 2: lfloor n/2rfloor leq |U_K| < n If n - |U_K| is odd, then consider the hyperedge V_K^p cup barU_K. All the vertices in this hyperedge are Blue, leading to a contradiction. If n - |U_K| is even, then consider the hyperedge U_K cup barV_K^p. At least one of the vertices, say v_l^p in barV_K^p, must have been colored by Blue in chi. Consider the vertex u_l such that (u_l,v_l^p) is a matching pair of vertices in (U,V^p). It can be seen that the hyperedge V_K^p cup barU_K cup \v_l^p\ setminus \u_l\ is Blue, leading to a contradiction. Box

nodes.statement: Our construction produces a hypergraph H with a monochromatic hyperedge under any given Red-Blue coloring of its vertices.
conclusions: Our construction produces a hypergraph H with a monochromatic hyperedge under any given Red-Blue coloring of its vertices.

nodes.clean_text: Our construction produces a hypergraph H with a monochromatic hyperedge under any given Red-Blue coloring of its vertices.

nodes.statement: Consider a Red-Blue coloring chi. Without the loss of generality, let us assume that the core hypergraph C is monochromatic in Red under this coloring chi. Note that the pair (u_1,v_1) is not combined with any hyperedge in the core hypergraph to form a hyperedge. It can also be noted that any other pair (u_i,v_i), inot=1, is combined with every hyperedge in the core hypergraph, and therefore both u_i and v_i cannot be colored by Red. item Case 1: If either of u_1 or v_1 is colored with Blue, then there is no pair (u_i,v_i) such that u_i and v_i are both colored by Red. This satisfies the condition of Lemma for the set-ordered set pair (U,V^1). Hence, it follows from Lemma that the hypergraph H is monochromatic under chi. item Case 2: If both u_1 and v_1 are colored with Red and if there does not exist any other pair of vertices (u_i,v_i) such that both u_i and v_i are colored with Blue, then it satisfies the condition of Lemma for the set-ordered set pair (U,V^1). Hence, it follows from Lemma that the hypergraph H is monochromatic under chi. item Case 3: Let us assume that both u_1 and v_1 are colored with Red, and there exists at least one other pair (u_i,v_i), inot=1, such that both u_i and v_i are colored with Blue. Consider the set-ordered set pair (U,V^i). It can be noted that there does not exist any matching pair of vertices (u_j,v_j^i) in (U,V^i) such that both u_j and v_j^i are colored with Red. Hence, it follows from Lemma that the hypergraph H is monochromatic under chi.\;\;\;\;Box\\

It can also be noted that any other pair (u_i,v_i), inot=1, is combined with every hyperedge in the core hypergraph, and therefore both u_i and v_i cannot be colored by Red. item Case 1: If either of u_1 or v_1 is colored with Blue, then there is no pair (u_i,v_i) such that u_i and v_i are both colored by Red. This satisfies the condition of Lemma for the set-ordered set pair (U,V^1). Hence, it follows from Lemma that the hypergraph H is monochromatic under chi. item Case 2: If both u_1 and v_1 are colored with Red and if there does not exist any other pair of vertices (u_i,v_i) such that both u_i and v_i are colored with Blue, then it satisfies the condition of Lemma for the set-ordered set pair (U,V^1). Hence, it follows from Lemma that the hypergraph H is monochromatic under chi. item Case 3: Let us assume that both u_1 and v_1 are colored with Red, and there exists at least one other pair (u_i,v_i), inot=1, such that both u_i and v_i are colored with Blue. Consider the set-ordered set pair (U,V^i). It can be noted that there does not exist any matching pair of vertices (u_j,v_j^i) in (U,V^i) such that both u_j and v_j^i are colored with Red. Hence, it follows from Lemma that the hypergraph H is monochromatic under chi.\;\;\;\;Box\\

Then, it follows from the p=1 case of Lemma that all the hyperedges formed in Steps (v), (vi) and (vii) cannot be non-monochromatic under the above condition imposed on chi. This contradicts the assumption that chi is a proper 2-coloring of H. Box\\

nodes.statement: Although the constructions given in this paper provide better upper bounds on m(n) for small values of n, it gives a weak upper bound for a general n. The first interesting open problem is to improve the upper bound on m(5) or to prove that m(5)=51.
